ap_biology-m01.stem: A student uses dialysis tubing, a selectively permeable membrane, filled with starch and glucose solution and placed in a beaker of water. After an hour, the water in the beaker tests positive for glucose but not for starch. What conclusion is best supported?

options.text: Neither starch nor glucose can pass through the membrane.
options.why: Glucose was detected outside the tubing.

options.text: Starch molecules are small enough to pass through the membrane, but glucose molecules are not.
options.why: The beaker tested positive for glucose, which means glucose crossed the membrane.

options.text: Both starch and glucose crossed the membrane because the membrane is not selective.
options.why: Starch was not detected outside the tubing.

options.text: Glucose molecules are small enough to pass through the membrane, but starch molecules are not.
options.why: Only the small glucose molecules diffused out of the tubing.

ap_biology-m01.stem: A student places dialysis tubing, a selectively permeable membrane, filled with a starch and glucose solution in a beaker of water and tests the water in the beaker for starch and glucose after an hour. Which additional setup would serve as the best control?

options.text: A beaker with starch and glucose but no tubing
options.why: Without the tubing the movement across the membrane cannot be tested.

options.text: A tubing filled with a more concentrated starch and glucose solution placed in the same beaker
options.why: A different concentration tests another variable.

options.text: A tubing filled with water only and placed in a beaker of water, tested in the same way
options.why: A control with water inside shows whether the tests give a result without the solutes.

options.text: A tubing filled with the same solution and placed in a hot water bath
options.why: A change in temperature introduces a second variable.
